record.paper_title: Open questions regarding the arrow of time
record.context_brief: Initial conditions for partial Schrödinger waves
record.original_question: Can the global intrinsic dynamics of the Wheeler-DeWitt framework determine the initial conditions of the partial Schrödinger waves that appear in the semiclassical WKB regime? Since the WKB approximation yields approximately autonomous matter-wave evolution along quasi-classical geometries but does not by itself justify an ensemble of trajectories, the unresolved problem is how the full, timeless quantum state fixes the initial data for the branch-dependent partial waves observed as evolving quasi-classical worlds.

evidence.quote: Note that this WKB approximation does not by itself justify an ensemble of trajectories, since it preserves the global superposition of all partial waves that evolve along different WKB trajectories
The global intrinsic dynamics would be required, though, to derive initial conditions for all partial Schrödinger waves, to be used in the WKB region of geometry (at some distance from the big bang).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider canonical quantum gravity coupled to matter fields, formulated through the Wheeler–DeWitt constraint
\[ \hat{\mathcal{H}}\,\Psi[h_{ij},\phi] = 0, \]
where $\Psi$ is a timeless wave functional defined on superspace (the space of three-metrics $h_{ij}$ and matter configurations $\phi$). In the semiclassical (WKB) regime, one writes
\[ \Psi[h_{ij},\phi] \;\approx\; \sum_\alpha A_\alpha[h_{ij}]\,e^{i S_\alpha[h_{ij}]/\hbar}\,\chi_\alpha[h_{ij},\phi], \]
where each $S_\alpha$ satisfies the Hamilton–Jacobi equation of vacuum gravity, defining a congruence of quasi-classical geometries, and each "partial Schrödinger wave" $\chi_\alpha$ is shown to obey, to leading order in $\hbar$, an approximately autonomous Schrödinger-type evolution equation along the WKB time parameter associated with $S_\alpha$.

Because the WKB ansatz preserves the global superposition of all branches $\alpha$, it does not by itself select an ensemble of trajectories nor prescribe initial data for the individual matter wave functions $\chi_\alpha$.

Problem. Determine whether the global intrinsic dynamics encoded in the full Wheeler–DeWitt state $\Psi$ (together with whatever boundary or regularity conditions are imposed on it, e.g.\ in the neighborhood of the classical singularity) uniquely fixes the initial conditions of each partial Schrödinger wave $\chi_\alpha$ to be used in the WKB region of superspace far from the big bang. Concretely: provide a derivation, from the timeless equation $\hat{\mathcal{H}}\Psi=0$ alone, of the initial data $\chi_\alpha\big|_{\Sigma_0}$ on a spacelike slice $\Sigma_0$ in each WKB branch, or prove that no such derivation is possible without additional structure.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches on the Wheeler–DeWitt equation and its WKB / Born–Oppenheimer semiclassical expansion (including work extending the expansion to arbitrary orders and addressing unitarity) show that while the leading-order emergence of Schrödinger-type evolution along WKB branches is well established, there is no widely accepted derivation of the initial data for the branch-dependent partial waves directly from the timeless Wheeler–DeWitt state. The question of how (or whether) the global quantum gravity state fixes these branch initial conditions remains a foundational open problem connected with proposals such as Hartle–Hawking and tunneling boundary conditions.

status_evidence.title: Wheeler–DeWitt equation
status_evidence.snippet: The Hamiltonian in the Wheeler–DeWitt equation does not determine the evolution of the system, so the standard Schrödinger equation no longer applies; boundary proposals such as Hartle–Hawking are introduced as separate inputs.
status_evidence.claim: Initial/boundary conditions in WDW are typically supplied by extra proposals rather than derived from the constraint itself.

status_evidence.title: Semiclassical approximation of the Wheeler–DeWitt equation: arbitrary orders and the question of unitarity
status_evidence.snippet: Born–Oppenheimer/WKB expansion of WDW yields Schrödinger evolution along quasi-classical geometries with corrections, but treats branch wave functions as inputs.
status_evidence.claim: Recent semiclassical analyses derive the evolution of partial waves but not their initial data from the global state.
